title: Rabbi Chiyya bar Nachman – Nechemyah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman reports that in Kohelet Rabbah, supplied locator פ״יב־ג, ד־ו, he expounded the verse “and the men of valor shall bend” — these are his arms; “and those who look through the windows shall be darkened” — these are the wings of the lung, from which the voice goes forth. In Vayikra Rabbah, beginning of chapter 18, the statement appears with “bar Nachman,” and Hyman cites this name also in Tanchuma, Sarah 7, and Kohelet Rabbah 2:15. In Bava Batra 46a: “Rav Chiyya son of Rav Nachman said: They taught this only of him”; but Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman.

notes.text: The supplied Kohelet Rabbah locator פ״יב־ג, ד־ו is retained literally rather than flattened to an established continuous 12:3–6 range. Its precise subsection structure remains unresolved, keeping the notice held. The source’s lung imagery, name variants and Chiyya/Huna distinction remain preserved.

The printed entry (Hyman, vol. II, p. 447) gives פ״יב־ג, ד־ו. In the consulted Kohelet Rabbah 12:3, the anonymous voice interprets the men of valor as the arms. Chiyya son of Rabbi Nechemyah says ribs and, later in the passage, interprets the darkened windows as the wings of the lung. The readings at 12:4 and 12:6 concern the kidneys and heart, and the throat, respectively. Vayikra Rabbah 18:1 attributes both the arms and the lungs to Chiyya bar Nachman. The consulted Tanchuma Buber, Chayei Sarah 7, has Chiyya ben Nechemyah. Kohelet Rabbah 2:15 has Chiyya bar Nechemyah. Bava Batra 46a has Rav Chiyya son of Rav Nachman in the craftsman case.
